body_markdown:
## Summary


**What this article covers: A clear comparison of the Fi collar and Life360 Pet GPS across GPS accuracy, battery life, escape alerts, subscription costs, and which tracker works best for families in 2026.**


### Who it’s for


-


Pet parents comparing GPS dog collars for the first time


-


Families looking for a tracker that fits into their existing safety setup


-


Dog parents with escape-prone pups or dogs who visit a dog sitter regularly


-


Anyone deciding between a dog-specific collar and a whole-family tracker


### Key Takeaways


-


The Fi collar (Series 3+) runs on LTE-M and multi-constellation GPS, with battery life reaching up to three months in standard mode.


-


Fi requires a separate subscription with a minimum six-month commitment; Life360 Pet GPS tracking is bundled with your existing family plan.


-


Life360 puts your dog on the same map as the rest of your family - people, pets, and things all in one app.


Your dog is a certified escape artist. One second they're flopped dramatically on the couch, and the next they've spotted a gap in the fence and made their great escape. If you've been there, heart racing, treat bag shaking, calling their name into the void, you already know the appeal of a GPS dog collar that offers live tracking and peace of mind.


Two names come up again and again when pet parents start searching: the Fi collar and[Life360 Pet GPS](https://www.life360.com/pet-safety?icid=blog_fi-collar-vs-life360) . Both promise real-time tracking and escape alerts. Both run on GPS and cellular networks. The differences, though, matter more than they might look at first glance, especially for families who want more than a standalone pet tracker.


This guide breaks down exactly how each one works, what the subscriptions actually cost, and which tracker makes the most sense depending on how your family lives.


#### One tracker, two dogs, no extra subscription.


Life360 Pet GPS is included with your Gold or Platinum membership, so tracking your dog never means paying for a second app.


[See Life360 plans](https://life360.onelink.me/JqZQ?af_web_dp=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.life360.com%2Fplans-pricing&pid=web&c=blog_fi-collar-vs-life360-pet-gps&deep_link_value=open)


## **How the Fi Collar Works**


The Fi Series 3 and Series 3+ are purpose-built GPS dog collars that track your pup's location using a combination of multi-constellation GPS, Wi-Fi, and AT&T's LTE-M cellular network. The way Fi manages battery life is genuinely clever: when your dog is home and within the designated safe zone, the collar relies on Wi-Fi for home detection rather than burning GPS. When your dog leaves the safe zone, cellular reporting kicks in. That automatic switching is why Fi's battery life can reach three months in standard mode under normal conditions, the best figure in the GPS dog collar category.


The Fi GPS unit attaches directly to the Fi collar band. You can also find Fi compatible collars from third-party makers if you want to keep a favorite band. The Fi mini is a smaller version that sits in a module you clip to a standard collar, making it a better fit for small dogs or those who find the full collar bulky. In testing, the Fi Mini held charge slightly longer than the Series 3+.


The Fi app maps your dog's location, tracks daily steps, monitors sleep, and ranks your pup's activity against other dogs in your city. The leaderboard is genuinely fun for competitive dog parents. The app also lets you set safe zones, and when your dog leaves one, you get an escape alert. The experience is polished and the hardware is rated IP68 for full submersion, so swimming, rain, and mud puddles are not a problem.


## **How Life360 Pet GPS Works**


Life360 Pet GPS takes a different approach from the ground up. The device is a clip-on GPS tracker that attaches to your dog's standard collar or harness. It runs on multi-constellation GPS, Bluetooth, and LTE cellular, providing real-time location updates straight to your Life360 app.


The big idea behind Life360 Pet GPS is integration. Your dog shows up on the same map as the rest of your Circle, kids, partners, parents, and Tile-tagged keys. There is no second app to check, no switching between your family safety app and a pet-specific tracker. Everyone who already uses Life360 sees the dog, right alongside everyone else.


Escape alerts work through Life360's Places system. You set up locations; home, the park, your dog sitter's house, and get notified the moment your dog arrives or leaves. Escaped Pet Mode sends an instant alert to your entire Circle, so the search isn't just on you. The Life360 Pet Finder Network takes it further by notifying nearby Life360 members with your dog's details and your contact info, drawing from a community of over[91 million](https://investors.life360.com/news-releases/news-release-details/life360-reports-record-q1-2026-results) users.


Battery life is rated up to 14 days on a regular charge, with a Reserve Mode that stretches to six months at reduced accuracy. The device is IP68 rated, water and bite resistant, and weighs 33.7 grams. It fits collar widths up to 1.25 inches, which works well for most medium and large dogs. The built-in safety light and chime are practical for late-night walks or when your dog has disappeared into the backyard shadows.


## **Subscription Costs**


This is where the two products look very different on paper and where Life360 wins for most families.


Fi requires a standalone subscription to function at all. Plans include a six-month prepaid option at $99, a one-year plan at $189, or a two-year plan at $339. There is also a one-time $20 activation fee per dog, and no multi-dog discount for existing members. If you have two dogs, you are paying full price for two separate subscriptions. Each Fi subscription is dog-specific and lives entirely in the Fi ecosystem.


Life360 Pet GPS is included with Gold and Platinum memberships. The Gold plan runs $14.99 per month, and Platinum runs $24.99 per month. Crucially, those plans also cover crash detection and emergency dispatch for your family, 24/7 roadside assistance, unlimited Place Alerts, 30 days of location history, and location sharing for everyone in your Circle. The Pet GPS tracker itself is $49.99. If you are already a Gold or Platinum Life360 member, adding your dog costs nothing extra beyond the device.


For pet parents who want only a dog tracker and nothing else, Fi's dedicated product may appeal. For anyone who also wants family location sharing, driving safety features, or emergency dispatch, Life360's bundled value is hard to match. You are paying for the whole family's safety and getting pet tracking included.


If you don't need live GPS tracking, the Life360 Pet Tag offers a simple way to help reunite lost pets with their families through a scannable smart ID tag that works with any collar and requires no subscription.


#### Two dogs on Fi? That's two full subscriptions.


A single Life360 Gold or Platinum membership covers multiple Pet GPS devices, plus crash detection and roadside assistance for your whole family.


## **Escape Alerts and Lost Dog Searches**


Both products take escape alerts seriously, and both deliver when it counts, though the reach of each search network differs significantly.


Fi's safe zone system works well. Set a boundary around your home, and you get a push notification when your dog crosses it. Lost Dog Mode triggers live GPS tracking immediately and broadcasts to nearby Fi community members. The limitation is scale: the Fi network is made up of Fi subscribers, which is a smaller pool than Life360's user base.


Life360 Pet GPS escape alerts go out to your entire Circle the moment Escaped Pet Mode is activated. Your people see it and can help without any extra steps. The Pet Finder Network alert reaches nearby Life360 members, a much larger group, given Life360's 91 million active users. For families with multiple adults already on Life360, the response to an escaped dog is immediate and coordinated.


## **Which One Is Right for Your Dog**


The Fi collar is the right call for pet parents who want a dog-specific product with elite battery life, a fun activity community, and don't already use Life360. It's especially well-suited to active dogs who take long hikes, working dogs in rural areas, and dog parents who love data on their pup's steps and sleep.


Life360 Pet GPS is the clear winner for families who are already using Life360 or who want one app that covers everyone - including the dog. The value is unmatched for existing Gold or Platinum members. Your dog's location sits right next to your kid's location on the same map, escape alerts go to your whole Circle automatically, and a community of tens of millions of people can help bring your pup home. The 14-day battery is shorter than Fi's multi-month runtime, so charging is more of a routine, but the tradeoff comes with a whole-family safety platform built in.


If you have two dogs, the math also shifts. Two Fi subscriptions add up fast. A single Life360[Gold or Platinum membership](https://www.life360.com/plans-pricing?icid=blog_fi-collar-vs-life360) covers multiple Pet GPS devices.


**Keeping your pup safe starts with knowing where they are.** Life360 Pet GPS brings your dog onto the same map as the rest of your family, with escape alerts that go to everyone who loves them and a Pet Finder Network backed by over 91 million members. Learn more about Life360 Pet GPS and see how it fits into your family's plan.


Your dog is family. Treat them like it.

## **FAQ**


### **Does the Fi collar require a subscription?**


Yes. The Fi collar cannot track your dog's location without an active Fi membership. Plans start at $99 for six months, with a one-time $20 activation fee per device. Life360 Pet GPS takes a different approach: pet tracking is bundled into the Gold and Platinum memberships your family may already be using, so there is no separate pet subscription to manage.


### **Does the Fi GPS tracker work internationally?**


Fi currently operates on AT&T's LTE-M network in the United States, with no coverage outside the US. Life360 Pet GPS runs on worldwide LTE GPS coverage, making it a stronger option for pet parents who travel internationally with their dogs or spend time outside the US.


### **Can small dogs wear the Fi collar?**


The Fi Series 3+ fits neck sizes from 11.5 to 34.5 inches and is not recommended for dogs under 10 pounds. The Fi Mini is lighter and attaches to a standard collar, making it a better fit for smaller breeds. Life360 Pet GPS is also a clip-on design that attaches to your dog's existing collar, which can work well for a wider range of sizes without requiring a specialized band.


### **How accurate is the Fi GPS tracker in rural areas?**


The Fi Series 3+ uses multi-constellation GPS with access to 78 positioning satellites, which helps in areas where part of the sky is blocked. In areas without cellular coverage, the collar stores data locally and uploads when signal returns, meaning real-time escape alerts will not fire until connection is restored. Life360 Pet GPS faces the same limitation, as any LTE-dependent tracker relies on network availability for live updates.


### **Can multiple people track a dog with the Fi app?**


Yes, though everyone needs to be added through the Fi app specifically, which is separate from any other family safety tools you use. Life360 Pet GPS brings your dog into the same Circle as the rest of your family, so anyone already on your Life360 account can see your dog's location without joining a second platform.


### **Do I need a separate app for Life360 Pet GPS?**


No. Life360 Pet GPS runs through the Life360 app your family already uses. Your dog's location appears on the same map as your Circle members and any Tile-tagged items, with no second app to install or manage.


#### Your dog belongs on the family map.


Escape Alerts, real-time location, and a Pet Finder Network backed by 91 million members, all in the app your family already uses.
